The **Briefing** page in the app (settings section `briefing`, see
`backend/schemas/settings.py` `BriefingSettings`) -- everything
`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news

metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old

section stay in sync by construction.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,

section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the

three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

section stay in sync by construction.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news

section stay in sync by construction.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

section stay in sync by construction.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

section stay in sync by construction.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news

section stay in sync by construction.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news

`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

section stay in sync by construction.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,

metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old

section stay in sync by construction.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,

metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,

metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old

section stay in sync by construction.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news

section stay in sync by construction.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

section stay in sync by construction.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the

`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

The PowerShell/Linux handlers can't open the settings DB cheaply, so the
backend mirrors the few values they need (health thresholds and metrics,
three spoken phrases, delivery) to `<data dir>/backend/briefing_mirror.json`
on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.

`daily_briefing.py` reads: which sections run and in what order, news
topics and window, tickers and spoken names, tabs, plain vs AI narration,
the narration prompts, the spoken phrases, and the system-health limits and
metrics. Edit it there, no code change needed. It replaces the old
`daily_briefing.yaml`: a `personal/daily_briefing.yaml` is moved into the
settings automatically the first time the backend or the briefing runs, and
renamed `.yaml.migrated`. `watchlist_report.py` reads the same `tickers` and
`ticker_names`, so "add gold to my watch list" and the briefing's Stocks
section stay in sync by construction.

on every save and at startup. No file means the built-in defaults.
